teaser.text: TE Connectivity sells the small but essential parts that let power, data, and signals move through modern equipment. Its dollar comes in when customers take delivery of those products, and goes out through materials, labor, factories, delivery, and the other costs of serving them.

stock.title: TE Connectivity stock forecast
stock.meta_description: TE Connectivity's stock forecast weighs bear, base, and bull cases, cash generation, growth drivers, and today's valuation.
stock.opening: TE Connectivity's weighted value reaches $252.94 in October 2027 and $305.78 in October 2029. It hinges on data-center and grid orders, automotive content, Chinese design wins, inventory stability, and profitable conversion.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains TE Connectivity's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could TE Connectivity's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast assigns 25% to the bear case, 55% to the base case, and 20% to the bull case. Data-center and grid orders, automotive content, Chinese design wins, inventory stability, and profitable conversion will drive the outcome. FY26 results on October 28, 2026, test the guidance and order visibility. Astrodyne’s expected closing by the end of calendar 2026 tests funding, integration, and profit contribution. Through FY29, restructuring savings must justify their charges and cash costs.

The forecast gives TE a probability-weighted value of $252.94 in October 2027, a 21% return including dividends from today’s $212.64. It rises to $280.39 in October 2028 and $305.78 in October 2029, equivalent to cumulative returns of 35% and 49%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for TE Connectivity?

paragraphs.text: The bull case requires profitable shipments from data-center and grid demand, Chinese automotive wins to ramp, and Astrodyne to integrate successfully. Higher utilization expands margins, cash funds larger buybacks, and valuation rises to $348.41 in October 2027 and $591.47 in October 2029. Its 20% probability reflects the number of successes required and the absence of proven acquisition returns.

blocks.heading: How much cash does TE Connectivity really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash flow after capital spending on factories and equipment. FY25 operating cash was $4.139 billion, while capital spending was $936 million. That produced calculated free cash flow of $3.203 billion.

A stricter view subtracts stock-based compensation because stock awards can dilute owners or lead to repurchases. On that basis, real free cash flow was $3.054 billion. TE’s own measure was slightly higher because it added back other items.

blocks.heading: Is TE Connectivity's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The table shows why rising free cash flow did not remove the need for financing discipline. In some years, dividends and buybacks exceeded that year’s free cash flow. That does not automatically mean distress, because TE could use existing cash, borrowing, or proceeds from selling assets, but it does mean the payout was not funded by that year’s operations alone.

blocks.heading: What could change TE Connectivity's dividend?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise in the base from $3.36 per share to $4.07. The bear holds the current annualized rate at $3.12 before cutting it to $2.81, while the bull reaches $4.29.

The base reflects the declared $0.78 quarterly dividend and approximately 10% annual increases. The bull requires faster cash-flow growth; the bear reflects acquisition funding and weaker conversion. Fiscal 2025 free cash flow was $3.203 billion, supporting the base, but the five-year dividend record was uneven.

earnings.opening: TE Connectivity reports fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results on October 28, 2026. The key watch is whether record orders and backlog become GAAP profit and cash.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers what TE Connectivity’s business, rivals, management, and risks are.

blocks.heading: What has TE Connectivity guided for fiscal 2026?

paragraphs.text: For fiscal 2026, TE expects adjusted EPS of $11.43 and GAAP EPS of $10.82. It guides to sales growth of 14.8%, including organic growth of 11.2%. Organic growth measures the performance of businesses TE already owned, excluding acquisitions, divestitures, and currency translation. The gap between reported and organic growth therefore shows how much comes from the existing business rather than changes in the portfolio or exchange rates.

blocks.heading: Has TE Connectivity kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: At Investor Day in November 2025, management projected 6–8% through-cycle growth and incremental margins above 30%. It also projected double-digit adjusted EPS growth. Those are promises to be tested, not results already delivered.

blocks.heading: How has TE Connectivity’s revenue and profit trended over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Operating income was $981 million and diluted EPS was $2.55. Quarterly operating cash was almost unchanged from a year earlier, while free cash flow declined. That gap directs attention to collections, inventory, and capital spending rather than allowing earnings alone to define the quarter.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in TE Connectivity’s next results?

paragraphs.text: TE is scheduled to report fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results on October 28, 2026. Investors will compare sales and EPS with both management’s guide and the slightly higher analyst consensus. They will also look for evidence that record orders and backlog provide genuine visibility into the next fiscal year, rather than demand that is delayed or cancelled.

The Astrodyne transaction is expected to close by the end of calendar 2026, subject to approvals and other closing conditions. Afterward, the important questions are how TE funds the purchase, how much sales and profit Astrodyne contributes, and whether integration disrupts customers or requires more cash than expected.
